findings.what: JT's 743929 advice ('best + its closest one-line neighbour, not diversity') ADDRESSED. (i) It agrees with the model against diversity: {#37,#38} and any two-lever-apart pair score lower than a one-line pair that keeps the robust lever. (ii) V_pub = exp79a has two one-line neighbours: exp70g (drop CI) and exp75 (cap 6 -> 4). JT does not say which line to toggle. The honest criterion is to toggle the lever whose private sign is least certain. That is cap 6 (R25P-4), so exp75 wins; exp70g wins only in cap-tight worlds. (iii) If V_pub becomes exp87a (K + CI), JT's literal neighbour is exp79a (drop K), but mc25 prefers exp75 (drops K and cap, the two public-selected levers, and keeps CI): G-F = +0.11 bronze and G-H = +0.05..+0.07 across K means +0.0002/0/-0.0005. This departs from JT's letter (two lines, not one) and says so. Reason: JT's neighbour rule is tuned for a public-winning file whose levers are all public-selected; ours carries two such levers.
